Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 14, verse 1:

(p-3704) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Surah Ibrahim.

It was named thus because it contains the supplications of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and it is completed with this creed (millah),

such as the Hajj and the making of the Ka'bah the qiblah of prayer. Together with the indication of its greatness, such that it became among the important matters agreed upon as the ultimate of the perfection of Ibrahim (peace and blessings be upon him), and upon the prophethood of our Prophet, upon whom be the most perfect greetings and the best peace, together with the ultimate of his perfection. This is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an! Related by al-Mahayimi.

It was revealed in Makkah, it is said, except for His saying, exalted is He: "Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief?" It has fifty-two verses.

(p-3705) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1] ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book which We have sent down to you, that you might bring mankind from darkness into light by the permission of their Lord, to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.﴾

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book﴾: "A Book" is the predicate of "Alif, Lam, Ra" if the latter is taken as the subject; or it is the predicate of an omitted subject if the latter is taken as a predicate of a hidden subject; or it is recited in the manner of enumeration. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿which We have sent down to you﴾, is a description of it. ﴿That you might bring mankind from darkness into light﴾, i.e., from misguidance to guidance. ﴿By the permission of their Lord﴾, i.e., by His command. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy﴾, is a substitute for His saying "to the light", by repeating the governing particle (al-'amil). Or it is resumptive, as if it were said: "To which light?" So it was said: "to the path of..." etc. "The Exalted in Might" is He who cannot be overcome nor resisted, but is the Subduer, the Capable. "The Praiseworthy" is He who is praised in His command and His prohibition, for His bestowal of the greatest blessings in both.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[2] ﴿Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.﴾

﴿Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾. The word "Allah" was read in the nominative, as the subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject of a nominal sentence), and its predicate is what follows it. Or it is read as a predicate (khabar) of an elided subject. It was also read in the genitive, as an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) to ﴿the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Ibrahim: 1]. ﴿And woe to the disbelievers﴾, i.e., because of what We sent down to you, ﴿from a severe punishment﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, which is the punishment of the Fire.

(p-3706)

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿Those who prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter, and bar (others) from the way of God, and seek to make it crooked. Those are in far-off error.﴾

﴿Those who prefer the worldly life over the Hereafter﴾ means: they give it preference over it. ﴿And bar (others) from the way of God﴾ by hindering people from faith. ﴿And seek to make it crooked﴾ means: they describe it as deviating from the truth and the correct path, or they seek to make its adherents turn back into apostasy, or they seek a crookedness in it, meaning they try to find in it a damaging flaw. This is by omission and conveyance (al-hadhf wa al-iisal, the omission of a preposition and its transfer to the verb). ﴿Those are in far-off error﴾ means: they have strayed from the path of truth and stopped far short of it. Distance (al-bu'd) in its strict sense belongs to the one who is astray himself, but it is ascribed to his action for emphasis (al-mubalaghah), by making the error itself be the one that is astray. The choice of the adverbial phrase "in" (fi) rather than the phrase "they are misguided with a far-off misguidance" (ulaika dallun dalalan ba'idan) indicates their being firmly established in it, as it encompasses them the way an enveloping thing encompasses what it encloses, for the sake of emphasizing the description of error. His saying, exalted is He:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[4] ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, so that he might make [the message] clear to them. Then Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, so that he might make [the message] clear to them﴾ means: so that they may understand from him what he calls them to, and so that they will have no proof against Allah, nor say: "We did not understand what we were addressed with," as He said: ﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail?"﴾ [Fussilat: 44]

If you say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not sent to the Arabs alone; rather he was sent to all people: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158]; indeed he was sent to both jinn and humankind, and they speak different languages. If the Arabs have no proof, then others have the proof. And if others have no proof, then if it had been revealed in a foreign tongue, the Arabs would likewise have had no proof? (I say): It is either revealed in all languages or in one of them. There is no need for it to be revealed in all languages, because translation serves in that stead and suffices to avoid prolixity. So it remains that it be revealed in one language, and the most fitting of languages is the language of the Messenger's people, because they are closest to him. When they understood him, grasped him clearly, and it was transmitted from them and spread, translations took up the task of explaining it and making it understood, as you see the situation and witness it in the substitution of translations in every nation of the non-Arab peoples, together with the agreement of the people of distant lands, remote regions, and differing nations and generations upon one Book, their striving to learn its wording and learn its meanings, and what branches out from that of sublime benefits, and what multiplies in exhausting souls and taxing minds in it, of acts of nearness and acts of obedience leading to abundant reward. Also, because it is further from distortion and alteration and safer from dispute and disagreement. And also, because if it had been revealed in all the languages of the two species, with their differences and multitude, and each one had been independently miraculous in its eloquence, and the Arab Messenger had addressed every nation in its own tongue, just as he addressed his own nation in which he was, reciting it to them as a miracle, that would have been a matter close to compulsion. The meaning of ﴿with the language of his people﴾ is with the dialect of his people, as stated in (al-Kashshaf).

Some of the verifiers said: One may ask, does this verse not indicate that the mission of the Prophet (ﷺ) was for the Arabs specifically? We say: No; because it is the custom of Allah to choose one nation and prepare it for refining the other nations, just as He prepares one individual from among them for refining the rest of its individuals. Since the Arab nation was the one chosen for refining the nations and correcting their crookedness and raising the banner of justice in that dark world, it became necessary that the divine refinement descend in its language specifically, until it became ready and prepared to discharge its function. Allah completed His favour upon it, and it stood up to what was entrusted to it in a manner that astonished the whole world, and for Allah in His creation are affairs.

Admonition:

Whoever holds that languages are conventional has used this verse as evidence. He said: For if they were tawqifi (divinely taught), they would not have been known except after the coming of the Messenger, whereas the verse is explicit that they were known before him.

And His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Then Allah leaves astray whom He wills﴾ mean: because of his engaging in the causes that lead to it, or He forsakes him and does not show him kindness, knowing that kindness will not benefit him. ﴿And guides whom He wills﴾ because of his turning in repentance and his facing toward the truth. (The fa' is) eloquent (fa' fasiha), as if it were said: "So they made it clear, and Allah leads astray whom He wills to lead astray and guides whom He wills." The omission is to signal that each messenger's hastening to what he was commanded, and the course of each of the people of forsaking and of guidance according to His custom, is a settled matter, needing no mention or explanation. ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ meaning: He is not overcome, and He decrees only what contains wisdom.

Then it is pointed out to elaborate what was stated in brief in His words: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people﴾ with His saying, Glorified is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5] ﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [saying]: "Bring your people out from the darknesses into the light, and remind them of the Days of Allah. Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful one."﴾

﴿And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [saying]: "Bring your people out from the darknesses into the light, and remind them of the Days of Allah"﴾ meaning: warn them of its events, which befell the nations before them, such as the people of Noah and Lot. From this comes the "Days of the Arabs" (ayyam al-'Arab), for their wars and battles, because the days are magnified through them. It has been said: "His days" are His blessings upon them, so the verse after it is an elaboration of it. It has also been said: they are more general than blessings and trials. The first view is better in my opinion, because each verse is specific to its context, and ta'sis (establishing a new meaning) is better than ta'kid (emphasis). In the iltifat (shift from address in the first person to the third person), by adding it to the Glorious Name, there is an announcement of the magnitude of its matter. Abu Bakr Ibn al-'Arabi said: this verse is in the admonition that softens the hearts.

﴿Indeed in that﴾ meaning: in the reminder of them, ﴿are signs for every patient, grateful one﴾ meaning: one who is patient under His trial and thankful for His blessings. So when he hears of the trials that Allah sent upon the nations, or of the blessings He poured upon them, he becomes alert to what is incumbent upon him of patience and gratitude. It has been said: he intended "for every believer," because gratitude and patience are the hallmark of the believer. The placing of "patient" (al-sabbar) before "grateful" (al-shakur) is due to the precedence of the object of patience, namely faith, over the object of gratitude, namely blessings, and because gratitude is the outcome of patience.

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[6] ﴿And when Moses said to his people, "Remember the favour of God upon you when He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who inflicted on you the worst torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women. In that was a tremendous trial from your Lord."﴾

﴿And when Moses said to his people, "Remember the favour of God upon you when He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who inflicted on you the worst torment"﴾: that is, they desired it for you. ﴿and slaughtered your sons﴾: that is, the male infants. ﴿and spared your women﴾: that is, they let them live. ﴿In that was a tremendous trial from your Lord﴾: the reference is to the deeds of the people of Pharaoh. Attributing it to God, the Exalted, means creating it, or enabling and empowering it. It has been said: that the slaughter of the sons was clearly a trial. As for sparing the women, who are the daughters, that is, letting them live, it was because they used them as servants and separated them from their husbands. Or it was because their survival without the sons was a grief in itself, as it has been said:

Of the greatest calamities, as I see it, is the survival of daughters while sons have died.

It is also possible that the reference is to the compulsion arising from that. And "the trial" (al-balā') means testing through blessing, and that is a tremendous trial.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "Al-balā' can be a test through blessing and through affliction alike. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiya': 35]. And Zuhayr said:

So he tested them both with the best of tests, which tests."

Therefore it was permitted that the reference be to everything mentioned, which includes both blessing and retribution.

A subtle point (latifa):

The scholars of meaning (ahl al-ma'ani) have pointed out the subtlety of the coming of ﴿yudhabbihūna﴾ here with a waw (conjunction), while in Surat al-Baqara it is ﴿yudhabbihūna﴾ [al-Baqara: 49] without it, and in al-A'raf it is ﴿yuqattilūna﴾ [al-A'raf: 141] without it. The narrative is one, in that where the waw is omitted, the intention is to explain and clarify the torment, so it is not conjoined, because of the complete connection between them. Where it is conjoined, as here, that was not intended. As for the torment: if by it is meant the genus, then slaughter, being the most severe of its kinds, is conjoined to it in the manner of Gabriel being conjoined to the angels, to alert that because of its severity it is as if it were not of that genus. If by it is meant something other than that, such as enslaving them and employing them in arduous labours, then the two are distinct, and the context calls for conjunction. It was also permitted that the conjunction here is for explanation, and as if the explanation, being more complete in conveying the intended meaning and clearer, were like something distinct, and therefore it was conjoined.

And His, the Exalted, saying:

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor], but if you are ungrateful, indeed My punishment is severe.﴾

﴿And when your Lord proclaimed﴾ means: He announced and made known with an eloquent announcement — from among what Musa said to his people —: ﴿If you are grateful﴾, that is, for His blessings, by directing them to that for which they were created, such as the intellect toward correcting belief in Him, and using all the [other] blessings in accordance with that requirement: ﴿I will surely increase you﴾, that is, in blessings. ﴿But if you are ungrateful, indeed My punishment is severe﴾, so that there will befall you from it what strips away those blessings and brings down the most severe retributions.

(p-3711)

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[8] ﴿And Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and everyone on earth together, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.﴾

﴿And Moses said﴾, that is, to his people: ﴿If you disbelieve, you and everyone on earth together, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy﴾, that is, He is free of need of the gratitude of His servants, and is praised with the most sublime praises, even if whoever disbelieves in Him disbelieves. This is an explanation of what has been omitted from the answer of (in) [the conditional], meaning: if you disbelieve, its consequence will return only upon you, for indeed Allah is free of need of the thanks of those who give thanks.

In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Dharr, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in what he narrates from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, that He said: "O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most righteous heart of one man among you, that would not increase My dominion in anything. O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease My dominion in anything. O My servants! If the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, stood in one plain and asked Me, and I gave each human his request, that would not decrease what is with Me except as a needle decreases when it is dipped into the sea." So glorified is He, the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

And His saying, exalted is He:

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 14, verse 9:**

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿Has there not come to you the news of those before you: the people of Noah, ʿAd and Thamud, and those after them, whom none knows but God? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands to their mouths and said, "We disbelieve in what you have been sent with, and we are truly in grave doubt about that to which you invite us."﴾

﴿Has there not come to you﴾, that is, concerning the punishment of those who disbelieved: ﴿the news of those before you, the people of Noah﴾ (p-٣٧١٢), that is, despite their great numbers; ﴿and ʿAd﴾, that is, despite their extreme strength; ﴿and Thamud﴾, despite their great fortresses and crafts; ﴿and those after them, whom none knows but God. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands to their mouths and said, "We disbelieve in what you have been sent with, and we are truly in grave doubt about that to which you invite us."﴾

Ibn Jarir said: "This is a continuation of the speech of Musa to his people, meaning: reminding them of the Days of God, by His vengeance upon the nations that denied the messengers."

Ibn Kathir said: "There is a point to be considered in what Ibn Jarir said. The apparent meaning is that it is a new report from God Most High to this community, for it has been said that the story of ʿAd and Thamud is not in the Torah. Had this been part of Musa's speech to his people, he would have related it to them, and there is no doubt that these two stories would then be in the Torah. And God knows best."

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and those after them, whom none knows but God﴾, is a sentence composed of a subject and predicate that occurs as a parenthetical clause (iʿtiraḍ, an interjected phrase that interrupts the sentence). Or ﴿those﴾ is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with "the people of Noah", and ﴿whom none knows﴾ etc. is a parenthetical clause. The meaning of the parenthetical clause according to the second view: "Has there not come to you the reports of the vast multitude, so numerous that it cannot be counted, so that you might take warning from them? Indeed, in that there is a lesson." According to the first view, it is an ascending progression (taraqqī), and its meaning is: "Has there not come to you the news of these and of those beyond them who cannot be counted?" It is as if He says: "Leave aside the detail, for there is no hope of it." In this there is subtlety, since it creates the impression of combining generality (ijmāl) and detail (tafṣīl).

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿they put their hands to their mouths﴾ may be understood with ﴿hands﴾ and ﴿mouths﴾ as the well-known bodily organs, or as figurative usage (majāz). Regarding the first, there are several views:

That is: they put their hands to their mouths and bit them in rage and vexation at what the messengers had brought, as in His saying: ﴿They bite their fingertips out of rage﴾ [Al ʿImran: 119]. Or they placed them over their mouths in laughter and mockery, like one overcome by laughter. Or they placed them over their mouths, gesturing to the prophets to desist and be silent. Or they gestured with their hands (p-٣٧١٣) toward the mouths of the messengers, telling them to be quiet; here "in" carries the sense of "toward". Or they placed their hands over the mouths of the messengers to prevent them from speaking. Or they seized the hands of the messengers and placed them over the messengers' own mouths in order to cut off their speech; whoever goes to excess in preventing another from speaking may do this to him. Or they gestured with their hands toward their answer, which is their saying: ﴿We disbelieve﴾, that is: this is our answer, which we say with our mouths. The intended meaning is their gesturing toward their own speech, as occurs in the speech of interlocutors, who gesture to signal that this is the answer and then affirm it, or affirm it and then gesture with their hands to indicate that this is the answer. It has been said that this is the strongest of the foregoing views, because when they tried to reject the messengers entirely, they combined in their rejection both action and speech. For this reason the particle "fa" (then, immediately) is used, to indicate that they gave them no respite, but followed their call immediately with denial. In their beginning the sentence with "inna" (indeed) and addressing the messengers with the pronouns of direct address, and repeating this, is an emphasis of great intensity.

As for the second, that is, the figurative meaning, there are several views:

Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: "The intended meaning of ﴿hand﴾ is what the messengers uttered of proofs. This is because conveying a proof is a great favour, and a favour is called a hand (yad); one says, 'So-and-so has a hand over me' when he has bestowed a benefit upon him. The word 'hand' may also be mentioned while its intended meaning is the transaction of sale or covenant, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed those who pledge allegiance to you pledge allegiance only to God; the hand of God is over their hands﴾ [al-Fath: 10]. Thus the clear proofs that the prophets, upon them be peace, mentioned and affirmed are favours and bounties (ayādin), and likewise the covenants that they made with the people are bounties. The plural of 'hand' in small numbers is 'aydi', and in large numbers 'ayadi'. It is therefore established that the clear proofs of the prophets, upon them be peace, and their covenants, may rightly be called hands. And since counsel and covenants only appear from the mouth, when they are not accepted they are returned to where they came from. The parallel to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When you received it with your tongues and uttered with your mouths what you had no knowledge of﴾ [al-Nur: 15]. Since acceptance is a receiving by the mouths from the mouths, rejection is a return into the mouths." End of quotation.

(p-٣٧١٤) In al-Razi there is a completion of the views, so consult it if you wish.

In al-ʿInaya it is said: "If you say: their saying ﴿We disbelieve﴾ is a categorical affirmation of disbelief, especially since it is emphasised with ﴿inna﴾, then their saying ﴿and we are truly in doubt﴾ contradicts it. I answer: the 'wa' (and) here means 'aw' (or); that is, one of the two matters is necessary, namely: we disbelieve with certainty, and if we are not certain, then we are at least doubters about it. In either case there is no path to acknowledgement." It has been said: disbelief is the absence of faith in one who is capable of it, so ﴿we disbelieved﴾ means ﴿we did not believe﴾, and this does not contradict doubt. Or the object of disbelief is the Books and the laws, while the object of doubt is what they are called to, such as monotheism. End of quotation. That is: their doubt about that does not contradict their definite disbelief in the former.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿mubīb﴾ means either "causing doubt", from "arābahu", meaning he caused him to fall into doubt; or "possessing doubt", from "arāba", meaning he became one possessing doubt. It is a descriptive adjective serving as emphasis.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[10] ﴿Their messengers said: "Is there doubt about God, Originator of the heavens and the earth? He calls you that He may forgive you of your sins and defer you to a specified term." They said: "You are not but humans like us. You want to avert us from what our fathers used to worship, so bring us a clear authority."﴾

﴿Their messengers said: "Is there doubt about God, Originator of the heavens and the earth?"﴾ That is: this is something in which there is no room for doubt, because of its utmost clarity.

Ibn Kathir said: This admits of two meanings. The first: Is there doubt about His existence? For the natural disposition (fitrah) bears witness to His existence and is inclined to affirm it, since acknowledging Him is a necessary matter in sound natural dispositions. But doubt and confusion may afflict some natural dispositions, so they require reflection on the evidence that leads to His existence. For this reason the messengers said to them, guiding them to the path of knowing Him: "[He is] Originator of the heavens and the earth," that is, the One who created them and brought them into being (p-3715) without any preceding pattern. The signs of their being originated, created and subjected are manifest upon them. Therefore they must have a maker, and He is God, there is no god but Him, the Creator of everything, its God and its Sovereign. The second meaning: Is there doubt about His divinity and His being singled out as the one deserving worship? He is the Creator of all existing things, and none deserves worship but Him alone, with no partner. For most nations acknowledged the Maker, but they worshipped others alongside Him from among the intermediaries whom they thought would benefit them or bring them near to God in nearness. End of quote.

We have previously discussed in the chapter of al-A'raf whether knowledge of Him, exalted is He, is necessary (daruri) or acquired (nazari); refer back to it.

The placing of the interrogative hamzah of denial before the adverbial phrase (fi Allah) indicates that the locus of denial is not doubt itself but its occurrence in a matter about which doubt is hardly conceivable at all. And the deviation from matching the reply to the speech of the disbelievers, who would have said: "Are you in a disquieting doubt concerning God?", is an emphasis on exalting the sanctity of His majesty above any trace of doubt, and a recording against them of the feebleness of their minds.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He calls you that He may forgive you of your sins﴾ means: He calls you to belief in His sending us, not that we call you to it from ourselves, as your saying ﴿of what you call us to﴾ [Ibrahim: 9] might suggest. The lam in (liyaghfira) is connected to (yad'u), meaning: for the sake of forgiveness, not for His own benefit, exalted and sanctified is He. Or it is for transitivity, meaning: He calls you to forgiveness, like your saying: "I invited you to Zayd." And (min) is either partitive, meaning: some of your sins, namely what is between you and God exalted, excluding wrongs against people; or it is a supplementary particle according to al-Akhfash and others, from its being added in affirmative speech; or it is for substitution, meaning: in place of the punishment for your sins; or the verb (yaghfiru) is taken to imply the meaning of (yakhlus, be freed).

Al-Zamakhshari claimed that it came with (min) in this way in the address to the disbelievers and not to the believers throughout the Qur'an. He said: This was to differentiate between the two addresses, and so that the two groups would not be equated in the promised outcome.

In al-Kashshaf he said: The restriction has another benefit, which is the differentiation between the two addresses by explicitly mentioning (p-3716) the forgiveness of all, while leaving part, in the case of the disbelievers, unmentioned, lest they rely upon belief.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and defer you to a specified term﴾ means: He will grant you a good enjoyment until a specified term. ﴿They said: "You are not but humans like us. You want to avert us from what our fathers used to worship, so bring us a clear authority."﴾ That is: a sign from what we propose, which shows your superiority over us through prophethood.

The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:

[11] ﴿Their messengers said to them, "We are only humans like you, but Allah bestows His favor upon whom He wills of His servants. And it was not for us to bring you an authority except by the permission of Allah. And upon Allah let the believers rely."﴾

﴿Their messengers said to them, "We are only humans like you, but Allah bestows His favor upon whom He wills of His servants"﴾ i.e., with the messengership and prophethood. ﴿And it was not for us to bring you an authority except by the permission of Allah﴾ i.e., by His command and will. And He did not will that, as in His saying: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾ [al-Isra: 59].

﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: It is a command from them to the believers in general to rely upon Allah, and they directed it at themselves first and foremost, commanding themselves with it, as if they were saying: It is incumbent upon us to rely upon Allah in patience over your opposition and what befalls us from you. Do you not see His saying:

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[12] ﴿And why should we not put our trust in Allah, when He has guided us to our ways? We will surely be patient over what you have inflicted upon us. And upon Allah let those who trust rely.﴾

﴿And why should we not put our trust in Allah﴾ Its meaning: What excuse do we have for not placing our trust in Him? (p-3717) ﴿when He has guided us to our ways﴾ That is, He has guided each of us to his path and his method (minhaj) which He legislated for him, and made it obligatory upon him to follow in religion. And since the harm inflicted by the disbelievers is of the kind that necessitates anxiety and agitation, which undermine trust (tawakkul), they affirmed it with an oath of emphasis, showing the completeness of their resolve: ﴿We will surely be patient over what you have inflicted upon us﴾ That is, from evil speech and contemptible deeds. His saying, ﴿And upon Allah let those who trust rely﴾, contains a concern with trusting in Him, Glorified is He, because the situation of the call (da'wah) requires it. For this reason it was repeated.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[13–14] ﴿And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely expel you from our land, or you will return to our religion." So their Lord revealed to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers. And We will surely make you dwell in the land after them. That is for whoever fears My standing [before Me] and fears My threat."﴾ [Ibrahim: 14]

﴿And We will surely make you dwell in the land after them. [18] ﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes upon which the wind blows violently on a stormy day. They have no power over anything they have earned. That is the far-reaching error.﴾

[18] ﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes upon which the wind blows violently on a stormy day. They have no power over anything they have earned. That is the far-reaching error.﴾

The word "mathal" (likeness, parable) is used figuratively for a description that contains something strange. God, exalted is He, likened their deeds, which they performed for their idols or to be seen by others, such as spending wealth and slaughtering camels for guests, in their being nullified—because they were not based on piety and faith—to ashes which a violent wind has scattered. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿They have no power﴾ and so on, is a resumptive clause; it serves as an illustration of the meaning intended by it and the summary of its aspect, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection they will have no power over anything of their deeds, that is, they will see no trace of reward from them, just as one cannot have power over anything of the ashes scattered by the wind.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The sufficiency with explaining the absence of any visible effect of their deeds performed for the idols, although these idols have terrible punishments, is to make clear the falsity of their belief and their claim that these idols are their intercessors with God, exalted is He. In this there is a mockery of them. In describing the error as "far" there is an indication of how far their error is from the path of truth, or from reward.

"Ishtadda bihi" (was intensified by it) comes from "shadda" in the sense of "ʿadda" (to count), and the "bā'" is for transitivity or accompaniment. Or it comes from "al-shiddah" in the sense of "al-quwwah" (strength), meaning it became strong through the accompaniment of carrying it. "Al-ʿasf" is the intensity of the blowing of the wind, and it is described by it as a time by figurative attribution, like "nahāruhu ṣā'im" (its day is fasting). The predicate of "mathal" is omitted, meaning: in what is recited to you. The clause "their deeds are like ashes" is a resumptive clause answering the question: "What is their likeness?" Or "their deeds" is a substitute for "mathal" and "like ashes" is the predicate.

This verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾ [al-Furqan: 23] And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The likeness of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind containing frost which strikes the crops of a people who have wronged themselves and destroys them. And God did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 117]

(p-3721) And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not nullify your charities with reproach and injury like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in God and the Last Day. **The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:**

[22] ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke it to you. I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me [with Allah] before. Indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment."﴾

﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided﴾, namely, the judgment of the salvation of the fortunate and the destruction of the wretched: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth﴾, meaning through the tongues of His messengers, that in following them is salvation and safety. That is, He fulfilled it and carried it out. ﴿And I promised you, but I broke it to you﴾, meaning: I promised you the promise of falsehood, which is that there is no resurrection and no recompense. And even if there were, your idols would be your intercessors. He did not state its falsehood explicitly, because of the indication of His words ﴿but I broke it to you﴾ concerning it. The word *ikhlaf* (breaking a promise) is used metaphorically for the non-realization of what he reported, and for his lying, or it is by way of *mushakala* (a rhetorical correspondence in wording). In the verse there is an eloquent conciseness resembling *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device in which two complementary elements are omitted from two places, each being indicated by the other). He first omitted "he fulfilled it" (*fa-wafa bihi*), indicated by his words afterwards ﴿but I broke it to you﴾ concerning it, since it is its counterpart; and he omitted secondly "the promise of falsehood" (*wa'd al-batil*), indicated by ﴿the promise of truth﴾.

﴿I had no authority over you﴾, meaning: no proof or evidence. ﴿Except that I called you, and you responded to me﴾, meaning: you hastened to obey me by this alone. That is, the messengers had established for you the proofs and the sound evidences for the truth of what they brought you, but you opposed them, and you went over to what you are in. ﴿So do not blame me﴾, meaning: for my promise to you, since it was not by way of compulsion. ﴿And blame yourselves﴾, meaning: since you responded to me by your own choice, when I called you without any proof or evidence, and you did not respond to your Lord, who called you with the call of truth accompanied by demonstrations and proofs.

Al-Qashani said: When the authority of the truth became manifest over the Satan of illusion, and he was illuminated by its light, he submitted, obeyed, and became one who adheres to the truth, knowing that the proof belongs to Allah in His call to the creation to the truth, not to him. His call to falsehood, through the adornment of the rulers (p-3725) and the embellishment of the worldly life for them, is weak and empty of proof. He acknowledged that His promise, exalted is He, of survival after the ruin of the body, and of reward and punishment at the resurrection, is true, and that He has fulfilled it. And his promise that there is nothing but the worldly life is falsehood which he invented. So the deserving of blame belongs only to whoever accepted the call devoid of proof and responded to it, and turned away from the call accompanied by demonstrative proof, and so did not respond to it. End.

It is related in *al-Iklil* from Ibn al-Faras that some people derived from this the nullification of *taqlid* (blind imitation) in belief. He said: This is a good derivation, because they followed Satan merely on his claim, and did not ask him for proof. So Allah related it as a censure of that act of theirs. End.

﴿I cannot help you﴾, meaning: I cannot be your helper or your deliverer from the punishment. ﴿Nor can you help me﴾, meaning: from what I am in. Ibn al-A'rabi said: *al-sarikh* is the one who seeks help, and *al-musrikh* is the one who helps. It is said: "So-and-so *sarakha*" when he sought help and said: "Woe, O help!" And *asrakhtuhu* means: I helped him. The *hamza* here is for removal, meaning: I removed his crying out, which is the prolonging of the voice. ﴿Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me [with Allah] before﴾, meaning: I disbelieve today in your associating me with Him before this day, that is, in the worldly life. So He, glorified is He, said:

The discussion concerning His words, may He be exalted:

[24-25] ﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word is like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and whose branches are in the sky? It gives its produce every season by the permission of its Lord. And Allah presents examples for the people that perhaps they may be reminded.﴾ [Ibrahim: 25].

﴿Have you not considered how Allah presents an example: a good word⌋ meaning, [its root] is firmly fixed in the earth, striking its roots into it; ﴿and its branches﴾, i.e., its highest part and its top, ﴿are in the sky﴾. ﴿It gives its produce﴾ [Ibrahim: 25], (p-3727) i.e., its fruit, ﴿every season by the permission of its Lord﴾ [Ibrahim: 25], i.e., by His will and His creating. ﴿And Allah presents examples for the people that perhaps they may be reminded﴾ [Ibrahim: 25], i.e., because in them there is an increase in understanding, admonition, and the depiction of intelligible meanings through perceptible forms.

The discussion of the meaning of His words, may He be exalted:

[26] ﴿And the likeness of an evil word is that of an evil tree, uprooted from upon the earth, having no stability.﴾

﴿And the likeness of an evil word is that of an evil tree, uprooted﴾ means: it is eradicated and its trunk is entirely removed. ﴿from upon the earth﴾ means: because its roots are near the surface of it. ﴿having no stability﴾ means: no firmness.

Note (tanbih):

In the thing likened (al-mumaththal bihi), that is, the tree, attention is drawn to noble qualities so that they may be considered in the case of the thing being likened (al-mumaththal lahu). Among them: that it is good (tayyibah), in the broadest sense, encompassing good appearance, form and shape, good scent, good fruit, and good benefit. And that its root is firm (thabit), that is, established and enduring, secure from being uprooted, cut off, removed, or perishing, so that joy and delight in it may be greatly magnified. And that its branch is in the sky, which indicates the perfection of the state of that tree in terms of the height of its branches and their strength in ascending, which proves the firmness of the root and the stability of its roots, and in terms of its distance from corruptions and filth, so that its fruit is pure, clean, and good, free of all impurities. And that its fruit is picked at all times, so its blessings and benefits never cease. There is no doubt that the presence of these qualities indicates the magnificence of the one described and the exceeding excellence of his virtue. The correspondence of this thing likened to the thing being likened, namely the truth, which is Islam, brought by the Seal of the Prophets, peace be upon them, is not hidden.

Since the parable was coined to contrast truth and falsehood in stability and its absence, and the intent is their people, he explicitly named both, so that this is clear for him, and said, regarding the people of the first parable:

(p-3728)

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[27] ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And Allah sends astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills.﴾

﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾ The "firm word" (al-qawl al-thabit) is the good word whose wondrous attribute has been mentioned, and it is the truth. Scholars permitted "with the word" (bi-l-qawl) to be connected to "keeps firm" (yuthabbitu) and to "believe" (amanu). On the first reading, the meaning is: He keeps them firm in remaining upon it, or He keeps them firm through it when they are questioned in the grave. On the second reading, the "ba'" is causal, and the meaning is: they believed in pure monotheism, so they affirmed His oneness and declared Him far above what is unfitting for His majesty. "In the life of this world" (fi l-hayah) is connected either to "keeps firm" or to "the firm," as Abu al-Baqa said. Al-Zamakhshari and his followers limited themselves to the first, when he said:

"The firm word is the word that has become established, through proof and demonstration, in the heart of its speaker, has taken root in him, so that he holds it as a belief and his soul is at rest with it. Their being kept firm by it in this world means that when they are tried in their religion they do not slip, as the People of the Ditch were steadfast, and those who were sawn apart with saws, and whose flesh was combed with iron combs. Their being kept firm in the Hereafter means that when they are questioned, at the gathering of witnesses, about their belief and their religion, they do not falter, nor are they confounded, nor are they bewildered by the terrors of the Gathering."

It was also said that its meaning is: steadfastness at the questioning in the grave. On the authority of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Muslim is questioned in the grave, he testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." He said: "That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word﴾." Narrated by al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and the authors of the Sunan (Ahl al-Sunan).

Based on this, the interpretation of "the Hereafter" is the grave, because the dead person is cut off by death from the rulings of this world.

He said concerning the people of the second parable:

﴿And Allah sends astray the wrongdoers﴾: that is, He creates in them straying from the truth upon which He kept the believers firm, according to their own will and choice. Their description as wrongdoers is because they place a thing in other than its proper place, or because they wronged themselves by altering the fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind. ﴿And Allah does what He wills﴾: that is, of keeping firm and of sending astray, as His perfect wisdom requires.

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 14, verses 28–30:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[28–30] ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for ingratitude and caused their people to settle in the abode of destruction? Hell, which they will enter, and wretched is the place of settlement.﴾ ﴿And they set up rivals to Allah to mislead [people] from His way. Say, "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾

﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for ingratitude﴾: it means the disbelievers of Mecca. The favor of Allah came to them, namely the Oneness [of God] (al-tawhid), faith, and guidance, through the sending of a Messenger from among themselves. So they exchanged its thankfulness for a great disbelief and a disdaining of it. ﴿And caused their people to settle﴾: that is, those whom they misled and turned away from guidance, and who followed them. ﴿In the abode of destruction﴾: that is, the perdition.

﴿Hell﴾ is an explicative apposition (ʿatf bayan) to it. ﴿Which they will enter, and wretched is the place of settlement.﴾ ﴿And they set up rivals to Allah﴾: that is, from among the idols, whom they worshipped. ﴿To mislead [people] from His way﴾: that is, from worshipping Him alone. ﴿Say﴾: that is, as a threat to those astray who lead others astray. ﴿Enjoy yourselves﴾: that is, in the pleasures of the worldly life. ﴿For your destination is the Fire.﴾

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[31] ﴿Say to My servants who have believed: establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, before there comes a Day in which there is no trade and no friendship.﴾

﴿Say to My servants who have believed: establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, before there comes a Day﴾ — this is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿in which there is no trade﴾, i.e., by which shortcoming may be made up, or by which one may ransom oneself. ﴿And no friendship﴾, i.e., companionship (khullah). It is a verbal noun with the meaning of companionship; that is, there is no ransom in it, nor does the friendship of anyone benefit by any intercession or leniency with wealth by which one might ransom oneself, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all, nor will compensation be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped﴾ [al-Baqarah: 123].

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, how did the command to spend correspond to the description of the Day as one in which there is no trade and no friendship? I say: Because people spend their wealth in contracts of exchange, giving something in return to take its equivalent, and in acts of generosity and gifts to friends, so that they may draw back gifts like them, or better than them. As for spending purely for the sake of Allah's countenance, only sincere believers do it, so they are impelled to it so that they may receive its recompense on the Day: ﴿in which there is no trade and no friendship﴾, i.e., no benefit in it through selling, nor through friendship, nor through what they spend of their wealth in exchanges and acts of generosity; benefit there comes only from spending for the sake of Allah. End of quote.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The apparent meaning is that (min) is connected to (anfaqu). The mention of the coming of that Day is to emphasize its content, in that each of the absence of intercession and of what makes up for shortcoming, whether by exchange or by voluntary giving, and the cutting off of the effects of the trade and friendship that occur in this world, and the lack of benefit from them, are among the strongest motives to bring about what its rewards remain and its benefits endure, by spending in His path, exalted is He. Or, because the hoarding of wealth and the withholding of its expenditure generally occur for the sake of trade and gifts. Since that is not possible in the Hereafter, there is no reason to hoard it until the time of death.

The specification of this emphasis is due to the inclination of natures toward wealth, and their being disposed to love it and to be tempted by it. It is not far-fetched that it is also an emphasis on the content of the command to establish prayer, in that neglecting it often happens through being occupied with trade and friendships, as in His words: ﴿And when they see a trade or amusement, they rush toward it﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 11]. When He had mentioned the states of the disbelievers regarding the blessings of Allah, exalted is He, and commanded the believers to establish the forms of obedience in gratitude for His blessings, He began to detail what necessitates for all of mankind persistence in gratitude and obedience for these great blessings, urging the believers toward them and rebuking the disbelievers who neglect them, who place disbelief and sins where they belong. So He, glorified is He, said:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[32] ﴿Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down water from the sky, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. And He subjected to you the ships to run upon the sea by His command, and He subjected to you the rivers.﴾

﴿Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down from the sky﴾, i.e., the clouds: ﴿water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾, i.e., by which you subsist: ﴿And He subjected to you the ships﴾, i.e., the boats: ﴿to run upon the sea by His command﴾, i.e., by His will: ﴿And He subjected to you the rivers﴾, i.e., so that they flow wherever you wish, for drinking, irrigation, and other uses.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[33] ﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constant (in their courses), and He subjected for you the night and the day.﴾

﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constant (in their courses)﴾ means: they persevere in their motion, their giving of light, and their dispelling of the darknesses, and in their setting right what they set right of the earth, the bodies, and the plants. ﴿And He subjected for you the night and the day﴾ means: they succeed one another, one following the other, for your livelihood and your rest.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[34] ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him. And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is [often] a wrongdoer and ungrateful.﴾

﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾: that is, whatever you need of that by which your circumstances and livelihoods are made right. It is as though you had asked for it or requested it through the tongue of your state (bi-lisan al-hal).

Al-Qashani said: ﴿of all that you asked of Him﴾ through the tongues of your predispositions (isti'dadat). For every thing asks through the tongue of its predisposition, and just as it is bestowed upon it along with the asking, without delay or lag: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾, because it has no end. ﴿Indeed, mankind is a wrongdoer﴾, that is: by placing the light of predisposition and the substance of permanence in the darkness of nature and the place of annihilation, and by diverting it therein; or by diminishing the right of Allah or the right of his own self by nullifying the predisposition. ﴿Ungrateful﴾, that is: toward those favors which cannot be enumerated, by using them for other than what they ought to be used for, and by his heedlessness of the One who bestowed them, and his veiling himself from Him through them. And the words of the Exalted:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[35] ﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this city secure and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols."﴾

﴿And when Abraham said﴾ means: remember the time when he said it, may God's blessings be upon him.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The purpose of this reminder is to recall what was said by him, peace be upon him, in detail. The aim is to reinforce what preceded concerning his, peace be upon him, astonishment at another kind of their offences: they disbelieved in the particular blessings granted to them after they had disbelieved in the general blessings. They also disobeyed their father Abraham, peace be upon him, who settled them in Mecca, may God exalt it, so that they would establish prayer, abstain from worshipping idols, and give thanks for the blessings of God, exalted is He. He asked God, exalted is He, to make it a secure city, to provide them with fruits, and to make people's hearts yearn toward them from every far-off direction. God answered his supplication, made it a secure sanctuary to which the fruits of everything are brought. Yet they disbelieved in those great blessings, exchanged the sacred city for the abode of ruin, set up rivals to God, and did what they did.

﴿My Lord, make this city﴾ refers to the Sacred City, Mecca the Honoured. ﴿Secure﴾ means: possessing security. Or, "secure" refers to its people. ﴿And keep me and my sons away﴾ means: distance me and them ﴿from worshipping idols.﴾

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:**

[36] ﴿My Lord, they have indeed led many of the people astray. So whoever follows me, he is of me; and whoever disobeys me, then indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿My Lord, they have indeed led many of the people astray﴾: that is, "You have made them a cause of their misguidance." It is said, "This world has tempted them and deceived them," pointing to the fact that he [Abraham] was tested through the idols by countless creatures. The clause is a justification for his supplication. He began it with the vocative to show his concern for it and his eagerness for it to be answered. ﴿So whoever follows me﴾: that is, in my creed, being a ḥanīf (upright monotheist) and a Muslim like me. ﴿he is of me; and whoever disobeys me﴾: that is, opposes my creed. ﴿then indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾: that is, indeed You are the Possessor of the Most Beautiful Names and of the Exalted Glory, the Self-Sufficient above all people. The specification of these two names points to the precedence of mercy.

[37] "Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they may be grateful."

"Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring" — i.e., some of my children, namely Isma'il and those born of him. (p-3734) "In an uncultivated valley" — this is the valley of Makkah. "Uncultivated" — meaning there is no crop in it. "Near Your Sacred House" — i.e., the one You have made sacred, forbidding that it be violated or treated with contempt. "Our Lord, that they may establish prayer" — i.e., so that they may perform Your worship in an upright manner in that place. This is connected to "I have settled" — meaning: I have not settled them in this valley except that they may establish prayer near Your Sacred House, and make it flourish by remembering You and worshipping You alone. The repetition and interposition of the address ("our Lord") serves to show the complete concern with the establishment of prayer.

"So make hearts among the people incline toward them" — i.e., hasten toward them and fly to them with longing, so that they will be at ease with them, become acquainted, form bonds of affection, and benefit one another. "And provide for them from the fruits" — i.e., so that merchants will bring them to them. "That they may be grateful" — i.e., for the blessing of their settlement near Your Sacred House, by praying in it, with perfect sincerity and monotheism, and with a free heart.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[38] ﴿Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we disclose, and nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven.﴾

﴿Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we disclose, and nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven.﴾ Because all of it is His creation: ﴿Should He not know, He who created?﴾ [al-Mulk: 14]

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is: You are most knowing of our circumstances, and of what benefits us and what harms us. You are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves and to our own interests, so there is no need for supplication and request. We call upon You only to manifest worship of You, to humble ourselves before Your greatness, to abase ourselves before Your might, to express our need for what is with You, to hasten to attain Your bounties, and out of longing for Your mercy. It is like a servant who flatters before his master, desiring to obtain his kindness, while the master is already fully disposed to good treatment.

(p. 3735) It is related from some of them that he raised his need to a generous person, but the success was slow in coming to him. So he wanted to remind him, and said: "One like you is not to be reminded," out of belittling him, or out of suspecting heedlessness regarding the needs of those who ask. But the one who has a need is not kept by his need from speaking about it. (End of quotation.)

It is also permitted regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and nothing is hidden from Allah﴾ and so on, that it may be part of His own speech, exalted is He, confirming Ibrahim, or that it may be part of the speech of Ibrahim, peace be upon him.

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[39] ﴿All praise is due to God, who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq. Indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.﴾

﴿All praise is due to God, who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq﴾ — i.e., that they should stand in my place in calling to Him, exalted is He, spreading the hanifiyyah (the pure monotheistic faith), and establishing the prayer after my departure. ﴿Indeed my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ — i.e., the One who answers it.

Al-Zamakhshari said: He mentioned the state of old age because the favour of granting a child is greater in that state, since it is a time when despair of begetting has set in, and attaining the need right after despair is among the most noble and sweetest of blessings in the soul of the one who attains it.

The commentary on the words of His Exalted saying:

[40] ﴿My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [among] my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.﴾

﴿My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [among] my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication.﴾ That is: my worship. Thus [it is stated] in (al-Tanwir).

(p-3736)

The commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[41] ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the day the reckoning takes place.﴾

﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the day the reckoning takes place.﴾ That is, the requital of the servants for their deeds. It was read as {wa-li-wālidayya} with the singular (wālidī), and it seems that this was before it became clear to him that (his father) was an enemy of Allah, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 14, verse 42:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[42] ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly.﴾

﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do﴾ means the polytheists of Makkah. That is: do not think, when He gives them respite and grants them a term, that He is unaware of them, neglecting them, not punishing them for their deeds. Rather, He keeps account of it against them and counts it against them with a precise counting. In this is consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ), a firm promise to him, and a severe warning to the disbelievers and all other wrongdoers.

﴿He only delays them﴾ means: by granting them respite, letting them enjoy their desires, and not hastening their punishment. ﴿until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ means: on which the eyes of the people of the place of standing will be raised up, because of the terror of what they see. So their eyes will not remain in their places, nor will they blink.

The discussion of the words of His saying, may He be exalted:

[43] ﴿Hastening forward, their heads raised, their gaze not returning to them, and their hearts empty.﴾

﴿Hastening forward﴾ means: rushing toward the summoner who calls them to the place of gathering (al-mahshar). This explains the manner of their rising from their graves and their haste toward the gathering, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Hastening toward the summoner﴾ [al-Qamar: 8], and His saying: ﴿On the Day they emerge from the graves in haste﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 43].

(p-3737) ﴿Their heads raised﴾ means: lifting them toward the sky. ﴿Their gaze not returning to them﴾ means: they do not blink, but their eyes are open and fixed, without moving the eyelids. ﴿And their hearts empty﴾ means: there is no strength in them and no steadiness, due to the intensity of terror.

Al-Zamakhshari said: al-hawa' (emptiness) is the void that is not occupied by bodies, and so it is described by it. It is said: "So-and-so's heart is hawa'," when he is a coward with no strength or boldness in his heart. It is also said of the fool: "His heart is hawa'." The meaning is that the hearts on that Day will have departed from their places, the eyes will be fixed, and the heads raised toward the sky, from the horror of that Day, its severity, and the fear of what occurs in it.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 14, verse 44:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[44] ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, "Our Lord, delay us for a near term; we will respond to Your call and follow the messengers." Did you not swear before, "You will have no cessation"?﴾

His saying: ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then those who did wrong will say, "Our Lord, delay us"﴾, i.e., return us to the world and grant us respite. ﴿For a near term﴾, i.e., a short span of time. ﴿We will respond to Your call﴾, i.e., by acknowledging Your Oneness and Your most beautiful names. ﴿And follow the messengers﴾, i.e., what they called to of the sharia.

﴿Did you not swear﴾ is governed by an implied verb of speech: it will be said to them, as rebuke and reproach, "You used to swear ﴿before﴾, meaning in the world, ﴿that you would have no cessation﴾, i.e., no passing from the abode of this world to another abode for recompense." This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that Allah would not resurrect those who die﴾ [An-Nahl: 38].

(p-3738)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 14, verse 45:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[45] ﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth for you the parables.﴾

﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves﴾ such as ʿĀd and Thamūd. ﴿And it became clear to you how We dealt with them﴾ i.e., through what you witness of the traces in their dwellings of what befell them, and what has come to you through successive reports of their news. ﴿And We set forth for you the parables﴾ i.e., the descriptions of what they did and what was done to them. That is: despite all this, there was no lesson (iʿtibār) for you in them, nor any restraint (muzdajar).

The commentary on His words, may He be exalted:

[46] ﴿And they had planned their plot, and with Allah is their plot, though their plot was such that the mountains would be moved thereby.﴾

﴿And they had planned their plot﴾ — i.e., against the Prophet, may the blessings of Allah be upon him. ﴿Their plot﴾ — i.e., the great one, in which they exhausted their effort to nullify the truth and establish falsehood. ﴿And with Allah is their plot﴾ — i.e., the recompense of their plot. ﴿And though their plot was﴾ — i.e., in its magnitude and severity — ﴿such that the mountains would be moved thereby﴾ — i.e., it was prepared and readied to remove the mountains from their places, because of its extreme severity.

It is permitted that ﴿in﴾ (in the Arabic ﴿إنْ﴾, in) be a negative particle, with the lam being emphatic for it. The meaning would then be: "It is impossible that the mountains should be moved by their plot," with the mountains being a parable (i.e., a metaphorical allegory) for the signs of Allah and His laws, since these are like firm mountains in steadfastness and stability. This is supported by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: {وما كانَ مَكْرُهم} ("and their plot was not..."). It is also read {لَتَزُولُ} with the lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida'), meaning: "It is of such severity that the mountains are moved by it and uprooted from their places."

(p-3739)

The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[47] ﴿So do not think that Allah would fail His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might, Owner of Retribution.﴾

﴿So do not think that Allah would fail His promise to His messengers﴾ means: of their victory, which is made clear in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51], ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21], and ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession in the land﴾ [al-Nur: 55], and so on.

Abu al-Su'ud favoured the view that the promise here means their otherworldly punishment of the wrongdoers, which was mentioned earlier in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He only defers them to a Day﴾ [Ibrahim: 42], etc. It is not hidden that the promise has been made clear in the last verse and the first two in their meaning, and clarification removes ambiguity. The second object, namely (His promise), is placed before the first, namely (His messengers), only to signal concern with it, since the verse is in the context of warning and threatening the wrongdoers with what Allah has promised them through the tongues of the messengers. Thus what matters in a threat is the mention of the warning. This is as stated in (al-Intisaf) by Ibn al-Munayyir.

In (al-Kashshaf), its being placed first is for the sake of giving it attention and because it is the intended point of the benefit. As for what he mentioned, namely those upon whose tongue the promise was made, it was mentioned only as a subordinate matter for clarification and detail after a general statement. This is from the style of ascent (*tarraqi*), as in His saying: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾ [Ta-Ha: 25].

﴿Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might﴾, that is, Victorious, who cannot be outwitted; ﴿Owner of Retribution﴾ against His enemies, granting victory to His allies.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[48] ﴿On the day the earth will be changed into a different earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾

﴿On the day the earth will be changed into a different earth, and the heavens﴾. That is because its mountains will move away from it, its seas will be made to burst forth, and it will be leveled, so that no crookedness or elevation will be seen in it. The heavens will be changed by the scattering of their stars, the eclipse of their sun, the darkening of their moon, their splitting asunder, and their becoming gates.

"(On the day)" is a substitute (badal, a grammatical substitution of one noun for another) for ﴿the day when the punishment comes to them﴾, or an adverbial of time (zarf, a noun of time functioning as an adverb) for "retribution", or it is implied as "(remember)" (اُذْكُرْ), or as "﴿He will not break His promise﴾".

"And they come forth" (وبَرَزُوا): that is, the creatures, or the wrongdoers, from their graves. "Before Allah, the One, the Subduer": that is, for His reckoning and His recompense.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The mention of the two attributes serves to magnify the matter, to instill awe, to show the falsity of polytheism, and to establish the retribution on that day if it is an adverbial of it. And it establishes the coming of the promised punishment if it is a substitute for ﴿the day when the punishment comes to them﴾. For when the matter belongs to One who overpowers, it is at the utmost of severity and difficulty.

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[49] ﴿And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles.﴾

﴿And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles.﴾ *Muqarranin* (مُقَرَّنِينَ) is the plural of *muqarran*, meaning one who is gathered in a *qaran* (قَرَن, with two fatha vowels), which is the bond by which something is tied. That is, He binds some of them with others according to their association in crimes and corruption, so that peers and similar types are joined together, each category with its own kind. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [Al-Saffat: 22], and He said: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [At-Takwir: 7]. Or (it means) they are bound together with the devils, according to His words, exalted is He: ﴿We will surely gather them and the devils﴾ [Maryam: 68]. Or (it means) their hands and feet are bound to their necks with shackles. His words, exalted is He, ﴿in shackles﴾ [Sad: 38], mean: in fetters or iron collars. *Al-asfad* is the plural of *safad* (صَفَد, with two fatha vowels), meaning a fetter or a shackle. The *qayd* (قَيْد, fetter) is what is placed on the foot, while the *ghull* (غُلّ, with a damma), is what is on the hand and the neck, and what binds the hand and the foot to the neck. The prepositional phrase (*al-jar*) is linked to *muqarranin* (مُقَرَّنِينَ), or it is a *hal* (حال, circumstantial accusative) from its pronoun, meaning: fettered. And His words, exalted is He:

(p-٣٧٤١)

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[50] ﴿Their garments will be of pitch, and fire will cover their faces.﴾

﴿Their garments will be of pitch﴾ is a comparison of them to the most hideous sight known among the Arabs: the mangy camels that are smeared with tar (qatran). It also informs that the greatest disease afflicting the skin is scabies, which breaks it out, and that the most wretched of remedies, because of its ugliness of color and smell, is tar, for it is black and foul-smelling.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The skins of the people of the Fire will be smeared with it until its coating on them becomes like garments (sarabil), which are shirts (al-qumas), so that four things combine upon them: the sting of the tar, its burning heat, the speed of the fire in their skins, and the savage color, and the stench of its smell, with the difference between the two tars being like the difference between the two fires. Everything that God has promised and threatened regarding the Hereafter, between it and what we witness of its kind there is an incomparable measure, as if what we have of it is only the names and the named things there. So by His vast generosity we seek refuge from His wrath, and we ask Him for success in what saves us from His punishment. End.

What supports what we have explained, that the verse indicates their being afflicted with the scabies of Hell, is what Imam Ahmad and Muslim narrated from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Four matters of the Jahiliyyah will remain among my nation, which they will not abandon: boasting about lineages, defaming of ancestry, seeking rain by the stars, and wailing over the dead. And the wailing woman, if she does not repent before her death, will be raised on the Day of Resurrection wearing a garment of tar and a coat of mange."

I have come across a treatise by Shams al-Bulaghaa al-Kharazmi, which he sent to someone who complained to him of the disease of scabies, in which he said: Scabies is an itch whose substance is dryness and heat, a fuel and an inflammation, and a soldier from the armies of affliction, which filth supplies, as dryness and heat increase it. It is an ailment that indicates neglect of the soul's due care and negligence in treatment and attention; it testifies that its owner is weak in resolve in guarding himself, a captive in the hand of greed and desire, deceiving his own self, and scant in preserving his spirit. This ailment brings its owner disgrace and shame, and causes him embarrassment and lassitude; he looks at people with the eye of one who is suspected, and hides from them as one hides a defect. Natures recoil from him, souls find him disgusting, and eyes turn away from sharing a meal with him. The least that befalls him is that he is deprived of the instruments of eating, which are his hands, and the instruments of meeting and visiting, which are his legs. And if there were no other subtle harms of it and no wondrous afflictions, it would still be that it ages youths, disfigures a person, and makes him unlettered after having been literate, and foreign-tongued though not foreign. His own self recoils from him, his bride flees from his bed, and the nearest of people distance themselves from him. Then it is a quarter of the quarters of abandonment and a portion of the portions of deprivation. The poet said:

May God protect you from four things: death, love, bankruptcy, and scabies.

And what is thought of a disease about which proverbs have traveled and sayings have been uttered beyond all other ailments?

Abu Tammam said:

When it saw its sister ruined yesterday, ruin became for it more contagious than scabies.

And Labid said:

Gone are those among whose sides one lived, and I remain among a remnant like the skin of a mangy camel.

Thus he made it the head of the ailments and described it as the utmost of afflictions. End.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and fire will cover their faces﴾, meaning: the fire will rise over them and envelop them, the fire which touches their bodies clad in tar. The singling out of the faces is because they are the most honored and noblest place on the outer body, like the heart within it, and for this reason He said: ﴿It rises over the hearts﴾ [al-Humazah: 7]; and because they are the gathering place of the senses which were created for perceiving the truth. Yet they turned away from it and did not employ them in contemplating it, just as the heart is the noblest of the inner organs and the seat of knowledge, which they filled with ignorance. Thus did al-Zamakhshari and Abu al-Su'ud convey.

The commentary on the words of His saying, may He be exalted:

[51] ﴿That Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾

﴿That Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned.﴾ The prepositional phrase (al-jarr wa-al-majrur, "the prepositional phrase") is related to a deleted element. That is: He does with the criminals what He does in order that He may recompense, etc. The word "soul" (nafs) is restricted to the criminal soul by the context (qarinat al-maqam), or it is general, encompassing both the righteous and the wicked. On this basis, it may be related to His saying ﴿And they will come forth﴾ [Ibrahim: 48], and what lies between them is a parenthetical clause (i'tirad); or it may be related to (tara, "you see"): ﴿Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾, meaning: the reckoning of all creatures on the Day of Resurrection, because no matter occupies Him from another matter. The entire creation, in relation to His power, is like one individual among them, as in His saying: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are not but as a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28]. Or the meaning is: His reckoning is swift, that is, its coming is swift, as in His saying: ﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near for them, while they are heedless and turning away﴾ [al-Anbiya: 1]. And His saying, may He be exalted:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 14, verse 52:

(p-3744) On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[52] ﴿This is a message for mankind, so that they may be warned by it, and so that they may know that He is but one God, and so that people of understanding may take heed.﴾

﴿This﴾ refers to the Qur'an or to the surah. His saying ﴿a message for mankind﴾ means: a sufficiency for them, because of the admonition and reminder it contains. His saying ﴿so that they may be warned by it﴾ means: so that they may be made to fear and be admonished by it against the crimes for which the earlier peoples were seized. ﴿And so that they may know that He is but one God﴾ means: so that they may reflect upon the proofs and evidences it contains, to the conclusion that there is no god but Him. The warning is mentioned first because, when they fear what they have been warned of, fear urges them to reflect until they reach monotheism, for dread is the mother of all good; this is what al-Zamakhshari conveyed. ﴿And so that people of understanding may take heed﴾ means: so that those possessed of intellects may be admonished by it, and thus turn towards what contains their salvation and their happiness.
